Description
本ポジションでは、ラストマイルの物流拠点であるDelivery Station（DS）およびSub Same Day（SSD）の新規開所プロジェクトを主導する上級エンジニアを募集しています。建築・電気・空調・衛生・消火設備の多分野にわたる設計施工監理を総合的に担い、発注者の立場でプロジェクトの安全管理・工程管理・コスト管理を遂行します。年間複数拠点の同時立ち上げにおいて、各プロジェクトの設計品質と短工期の両立を図りながら、竣工・引き渡しまで一貫してリードします。安全管理では、工事請負業者が各種法令およびAmazonの工事安全基準を遵守できるよう、作業計画段階でのリスクアセスメントから工事期間中の安全パトロールまで一連の安全活動を推進します。万一の事故・災害発生時には再発防止策を立案し、工事安全基準へ反映するとともに全工事現場への水平展開を行います。工程管理・コスト管理では、複数の専門工事業者間の全体工程を調整し、コスト交渉を主導して予算内での竣工を実現します。さらに、過去のプロジェクト実績やデータを活用し、設計仕様・施工プロセスの標準化や簡素化を自ら提案・推進することで、拠点展開のスピードとコスト効率を継続的に改善します。社内の関連部門（オペレーション、調達、安全衛生等）と連携しながら、チームメンバーへの技術的なサポートも行い、部署全体のプロジェクト推進力の向上に貢献します。

職務記述（内容、責任、遂行要件、他職務との関係等）
70% ― DS・SSD新規開所の設計施工監理
・テナント物件の現地調査・設計要件の整理から、基本設計・実施設計のレビュー、施工監理、竣工検査・引き渡し
・建築・電気・空調・衛生・消火設備の各専門工事業者との工程調整およびコスト交渉
・工事請負業者に対する安全管理（リスクアセスメント、安全パトロール、是正指示）
15% ― 設計仕様・施工プロセス・安全管理の標準化
・DS・SSD向け設計標準（建屋仕様・設備仕様）の策定・改定
・施工プロセスや安全管理手順の標準化・ドキュメント整備
・過去プロジェクトの振り返りを通じたベストプラクティスの体系化
15% ― 予算管理・コスト最適化
・プロジェクト予算の策定・実績管理・差異分析
・VE（バリューエンジニアリング）提案によるコスト削減施策の立案・実行
・予算実績データの蓄積と、次期プロジェクトへのフィードバック

Related information
・所属部門:オペレーション技術開発
・職種:エンジニア
・勤務地:東京オフィス
・オペレーション技術開発部門の社員インタビューはこちら
・エンジニア職の社員インタビュー
オペレーション技術開発(JCFS)部門/東京オフィス勤務の社員S.U.さん
オペレーション技術開発(JCFS)部門/関東DS勤務の社員M.U.さん

Amazonは多様かつインクルーシブな職場づくりを目指しています。Amazonは男女雇用機会均等法を順守しています。人種、出身国、性別、性的指向、障がい、年齢、その他の属性によって差別することなく、平等に採用選考の機会を提供しています。障がいをお持ちの方は、以下をご覧ください。https://www.amazon.jobs/disability/jp

Key job responsibilities
DSおよびSSDの新規開所プロジェクトにおいて、建築・電気・空調・衛生・消火設備の複合的な設計業務を行い、工事フェーズでは常に安全を最優先し計画通りにプロジェクトを完了させます。同時に複数のプロジェクトを担当することもあり、社内外および海外の関係者と協力し円滑にプロジェクトを進めます。優れたコミュニケーション能力と、折衝力を持ち合わせていることが求められます。また、自身の豊富な経験と高い技術力をもって、組織内の技術力向上に取り組み、他のチームメンバーの育成など組織力強化を実現していきます。

A day in the life
DSおよびSSDの新規開所プロジェクトを担当していただきます。計画フェーズでは、自身の担当プロジェクトの実施承認を得るために、ソリューション提案、コスト、スケジュールなどの計画をまとめます。工事フェーズでは自ら現場で管理を行い、計画通り進捗しているか確認します。部内定例ミーティングとチームミーティングがそれぞれ週1回開催されており、そこで情報共有やチームビルドを図っています。出張など所属サイト以外での勤務は平均すると週1回程度あり、遠隔地の場合は宿泊を伴う出張もあります。フレックス勤務を導入し、個人のライフイベントを迎えながらキャリアを長期的に築いていける環境もあります。

About the team
Facility Design & Construction(建築設計・工事監理部)は、Amazonに必要な物流拠点の新規立ち上げ、また、運用中拠点の大規模な改修工事を担い、ビジネスやカスタマーに貢献するチームです。新規立ち上げでは、建物のレイアウトや建築、設備の設計を行い、プロジェクト全体の工程を守り、コスト管理を行いながら安全で生産性の高い建物を作ります。既存の改修工事では、生産性向上のための設備変更や、経年による老朽化対策の設備更新などを企画し、プロジェクトのオーナーとして品質、コスト管理しながら完了までリードします。今回の募集ポジションでは新規DS、SSDの工事を担当いただきますが、設計標準の最適化や工事管理の標準化など部内全体で行う業務にも取り組んでいただきます。

Basic qualifications

- 建築、電気、空調、衛生、防災設備についての一級施工管理技士（建築・電気・管工事）同等の知識
- 発注者側での7年以上の工事監理経験、もしくは請負工事会社での7年以上の施工管理経験
- 諸官庁と建築基準法や消防法、その他建築・設備に関わる法規に関わる折衝やProjectをリードした経験
- ビジネスレベルの日本語力（会議が進行できる、ビジネス文書がかける）
- PCスキル（Word, Excel, Power point）

Preferred qualifications

- 大規模な新築・改修工事現場での施工管理経験者　延床3万㎡以上
- 新築現場で受注金額が10億円以上、改修工事で5億円以上の工事について現場代理人、主任技術者経験
- CADでの作図経験およびPCスキル（Auto CAD）
- ビジネスレベルの日本語力・英語力（会議が進行できる、ビジネス文書がかける）
- 常にお客様目線で行動できる
- 論理的な思考力、優先順位の判断力および問題解決能力を持っている
- 迅速に業務をこなし、状況の変化に柔軟に対応できる
- 指示を待つのではなく、自分で考えて行動できる
- 新しい知識を学ぶことに対する意欲
- 企業のなかで起業している感覚を持って、常に情熱を持って取り組める
- 業者とのPartnership構築能力および優れた交渉能力を持っている
- 職場全体への貢献　他人の仕事をうまく進められるように情報を共有し、サポートする
- 多様性に富んだグループで働くことに対して前向きである

title: DCEO Facility Manager, ADC InfraOps DCEO
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Data Center Facility Manager to serve as a technical resource and leader within Amazon data centers. The position will help ensure overall availability and reliability to meet or exceed defined service levels of data center operations. The Data Center Facility Manager is responsible for the overall operation and maintenance of all electrical, mechanical, and HVAC equipment within the data center. The Data Center Facility Manager will assist in maintaining a high reliability and performance while keeping operating costs in facilities at a minimum. This equipment supports mission-critical servers and must maintain better than 99.999% uptime.

This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including electrical support equipment such as stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems that include but not limited to switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAC units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire suppression systems, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility.

Key job responsibilities
- Oversee all aspects of the data center's critical physical infrastructure. Ensure that all work performed within the space is done to high quality and without impact to internal/external customers
- Manage teams of 24x7 engineering technicians in all facets of their career
- Engage in improvement projects, often requiring reaching out to a variety of support teams, and drive them from conception to completion
- Coordinates daily with a multitude of third party vendors ensuring adherence to contracted SLAs
- Effectively and efficiently manage the operations budget and expenditures
- Routinely operate as the afterhours on-call Data Center Facility Manager for the data centers in the region. This will include responding to any issues within the data centers and managing the investigation, mitigation, and recovery of the issue(s).

Physical Requirements:
- Walk jobsites in uneven terrain.
- Work at heights and from ladders.
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or craw.
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 49 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 50 pounds or more.
- Carry objects weighing up to 49 pounds for short distances
- Work shifts longer than eight hours in duration.
- Respond to off hour emergency calls.
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Coordinate body movements when using tools or equipment
- Reach and stretch to position equipment and fixtures while maintaining balance
- Bend or twist the body into unusual positions while working
- Perform physical tasks all day without becoming overly tired
- Use hands to manipulate small wires and objects
- Apply force quickly to objects and equipment
- Push or pull heavy objects into position
- Work in a noisy environment
- Work at depths, such as under raised floors

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of management/team lead function experience
- 3+ years of work in data centers with an emphasis on building and equipment operation experience
- Experience with Microsoft Office products and applications
- Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret with SCI eligibility or above

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- 4+ years of work in a management position with 5 or more direct reports experience
- Experience in root cause analysis and troubleshooting or problem solving
- Experience in reading and understanding schematics and building drawings

title: Sr Manager, Professional Services Cloud Architecture, AWS Professional Services
descriptionHtml:
The Senior Manager, Professional Services Cloud Architects (PCAM) leads a team of 8–10 ProServe Cloud Architects (PCAs) within North America. Reporting to the Senior PCAM NAMER Lead, this role combines hands-on customer engagement with frontline people leadership — coaching PCAs through complex, ambiguous customer situations and driving them to successful outcomes.

This leader is deeply collaborative: partnering with peer PCA Managers, the NAMER leadership team, ProServe Account Executives, Delivery Teams, AGS Sales, and Solution Architect Leadership to accelerate customers’ cloud journeys. The ideal candidate brings a strong identity in building collaborative culture, thrives in ambiguity, and is passionate about developing technical talent while staying close to customers.


Key job responsibilities
People Leadership & Talent Development
- Directly manage a team of 8–10 PCAs, fostering technical excellence, customer obsession, and a collaborative team culture
- Lead performance management, career development, goal setting, and regular 1:1 coaching
- Drive hiring, onboarding, and retention to build and maintain a high-performing team
- Identify and develop future leaders; ensure team certification compliance
- Create an inclusive environment where PCAs can grow, take risks, and learn from ambiguity
Hands-On Customer & Stakeholder Engagement
- Serve as a hands-on technical and strategic advisor alongside PCAs in complex customer engagements
- Build trusted relationships with customers and partners, engaging at the executive level when needed
- Act as an escalation point for technical and commercial challenges within the team's portfolio
- Champion customer satisfaction (CSAT) improvements across all engagements
Collaboration & Cross-Functional Partnership
- Partner closely with peer PCA Managers to share best practices, balance workloads, and maintain consistency across NAMER
- Collaborate with the NAMER leadership team on regional strategy, coverage planning, and organizational initiatives
- Work with ProServe Account Executives, Delivery Teams, and AGS Sales to ensure seamless pre-sales to delivery handoffs
- Foster knowledge sharing, reusable artifact creation, and community of practice participation
Business Performance
- Drive Billable Bookings performance through team enablement, opportunity coaching, and strategic deal support
- Optimize Engagement Margin (As Sold vs. As Delivered) through quality solution design and right-sized scoping
- Monitor deal velocity, reduce concessions, and identify cross-sell/upsell opportunities
- Champion AI adoption with customers and builders
Operational Excellence
- Track and improve team KPIs: bookings, margin, CSAT, PCA development, and operational metrics
- Drive improvements in Engagement Velocity Acceleration (EvA) and delivery readiness
- Ensure team adherence to ProServe processes, tools, and quality standards

A day in the life
As a PCA Manager, no two days look the same, but every day centers on people, customers, and collaboration:

- Engaging with stakeholders across ProServe, AGS Sales, and partner organizations

- Working directly with customers to understand their cloud journey and unblock progress

- Supporting, guiding, mentoring, and enabling PCAs for success in their engagements

- Direct engagement with ProServe Account Executives (PAEs) to align on opportunity strategy and customer outcomes

- Participating in cross-organizational leadership and management forums

- Meeting customers and stakeholders where they are, whether that is a strategic planning session or a hands-on technical review

- Collaborating heavily with internal and external partners to drive shared outcomes

- Providing a consistent, collaborative bridge across the ProServe sales process, enabling strong relationships between PAEs and PCAs

- Helping to guide and train PCAs to increase engineering maturity and technical depth

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of IT and/or Management Consulting, or 5+ years of people leadership experience
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Math, or a related field
- 3+ years of people leadership experience
- Experience working with and influencing senior level stakeholders
- Experience working in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment, or experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects
- Experience in guiding, training and mentoring others, or experience working with customers with a passion for delivering exceptional service

Preferred qualifications

- AWS certification
- 5+ years of cloud computing experience
- Experience building and operating a cloud-based architecture
- AWS Professional level certification, or 1+ years of cloud architecture and solution implementation experience
- Experience working in a matrixed organization

title: Senior ProServe Sales Manager, Automotive & Manufacturing, Professional Services, Auto & Mfg
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced technology sales leader to join our AWS Professional Services (ProServe) team and help shape the future of automotive and manufacturing in EMEA. In this role, you will partner with our most strategic automotive and manufacturing customers to design transformative programs focused on AI/GenAI/Agentic AI, IT modernization, and cloud migration.

You will serve as a trusted advisor to C-suite executives and SVPs across Digital, IT, AI, and key business functions, from Manufacturing Operations to R&D/Engineering to Supply Chain to Connected Vehicle platforms. Working alongside ProServe sales, delivery teams, and specialist groups, you will design solutions that achieve meaningful business outcomes for our customers.

This role combines leadership and hands-on engagement. You will guide and coach your team while directly developing large, programmatic deals for selected accounts. Success in this position is measured through revenue, billable bookings, team engagement, and customer satisfaction (NPS, CSAT).

We are seeking leaders who can work backwards from automotive and manufacturing customer outcomes to design ambitious technology transformation programs. You will thrive here if you think big and innovate, obsess over customer objectives, execute at a high standard, and bring continuous curiosity to your work. A proven track record of growing businesses is essential.

This is your opportunity to shape how technology drives business transformation across automotive and manufacturing, from the factory floor to software-defined vehicle platforms to next-generation supply chains. You will be part of a global team of experts who help customers realize their desired business outcomes through AWS solutions and services.

Key job responsibilities
- Leading and developing a high-performing team of ProServe Account Executives focused on the automotive and manufacturing vertical
- Developing and implementing sales strategies to meet team targets and drive revenue growth across OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and manufacturing enterprises
- Cultivating executive customer relationships, earning trust and credibility, and shaping new opportunities for cloud transformation, GenAI adoption, and IT modernization
- Leveraging deep AWS knowledge to guide sellers in proposing optimal solutions that work backwards from customers' business objectives
- Monitoring and analyzing key performance indicators and driving executional rigor, accurate forecasting, and reporting to optimize operational processes and manage risk
- Partnering with ProServe delivery leaders, Solution Architects, and Forward Deployed Engineers to scope and shape complex, multi-year transformation programs
- Driving pipeline generation and deal progression through disciplined execution, structured account planning, and cross-functional collaboration

A day in the life
This is a customer-facing role. You will partner with C-suite leaders across major OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and manufacturing enterprises to scope and sell complex cloud transformation programs. You will be a player-coach for your team of ProServe Account Executives on consultative selling, review pipeline health, and collaborate closely with ProServe delivery leaders, Solution Architects, and the GenAI Innovation Center to shape solutions spanning connected vehicles, smart manufacturing, supply chain optimization, and AI/ML at scale. You will balance strategic account planning with operational rhythm, ensuring accurate forecasting and high customer satisfaction.

About the team
The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts who help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using AWS solutions and services. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute technology transformations and enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our Automotive and Manufacturing practice focuses on driving cloud adoption across OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and discrete/process manufacturers, with deep expertise in connected vehicles, smart manufacturing, supply chain optimization, and AI/ML at scale. We operate at the intersection of industry knowledge and cloud technology, helping our customers turn complex business challenges into competitive advantages.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in full sales cycle, technology sales, sales engineering/consulting or equivalent business development
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
- Experience in cloud computing technologies
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience with customer relationship management, especially C-suite level customer engagement
- Experience in technology/software sales, pre-sales, or consulting
- 5+ years of solving problems with technology in the Automotive or Manufacturing industry
- 7+ years of consulting sales and 3+ years of management experience

Preferred qualifications

title: Sr. SDE, Agentic Systems, Technical Content Experience (TCX) Engineering
descriptionHtml:
AWS Documentation, one of the most visited technical documentation sites in the world, is increasingly authored using AI agents; not as an experiment, but in production. You'll be the senior engineer owning the architecture behind it: a runtime that executes documentation workflows autonomously, multi-agent orchestrated authoring tools that help service teams produce documentation from their design documents and service models, and analyzers that review those contents against AWS standards before commit.

This is hard in interesting ways: agent that writes plausible-sounding API documentation is worse than no agent at all, so correctness and verifiability sit at the heart of the architecture. You'll decide how specialized agents divide work versus deterministic orchestration with agentic reasoning at the leaves, how their output gets evaluated, and when a workflow needs to escalate to a human. In a domain where agent patterns change every few months, you know that today's right call has a short shelf life and adapt your own orchestration patterns, tool ecosystem design, and inference cost and latency.

Shape technical strategy where ambiguity spans both product shape and technical approach, lead initiatives through engineers and teams you don't control, and ship weekly while doing it.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the architecture across the portfolio — hosted agent runtime, multi-agent authoring workflows, commit-time content analyzers, and operational telemetry — making technology choices where neither the product shape nor the technical approach is defined
- Design the correctness and verifiability layer: ground agent output in authoritative sources, catch fabrication, and define when a workflow escalates to human review
- Lead projects requiring work from multiple engineers, including agent orchestration patterns, evaluation frameworks, bidirectional XML transformation, and developer-facing authoring tools
- Turn content quality evaluations into feedback signals that measurably improve agent behavior, and influence architectural decisions in adjacent systems your services depend on but don't control
- Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, exemplary code, and mentoring engineers newer to production AI systems, while identifying root causes of systemic issues and balancing delivery speed against long-term system quality

A day in the life
You'll start with yesterday's agent runs - did the research agent find the right sources, did the writing agent produce content that passes style review? You're asking whether the orchestration architecture still holds as model capabilities shift.

Mid-morning, a service team needs documentation generated from a model type your pipeline doesn't handle. Neither the product shape nor the approach is obvious, so you design the pattern and prototype it.

After lunch, a partner team's API redesign affects how your agents integrate. You influence that design to serve both human and agentic workflows - building consensus without owning it.

About the team
The Applied Science team builds the AI-powered tools that are fundamentally changing how AWS documentation gets created. We develop and operate multi-agent content generation systems, intelligent code-review analyzers, developer-facing authoring tools, and the telemetry infrastructure that measures it all.

Our tools are used daily by hundreds of contributors across AWS. We move fast — shipping improvements weekly — while maintaining the reliability that production content systems require. The team values pragmatic engineering, measurable impact, and the intellectual honesty to know when an AI approach isn't working and to try something else.

We're part of TCX Engineering, the organization behind the AWS Documentation website and the AI-first content platform powering it. You'll work closely with product managers, content strategists, and peer engineering teams building the broader platform infrastructure.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in computer science or equivalent
- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems
- Experience with Machine Learning and Large Language Model fundamentals, including architecture, training/inference lifecycles, and optimization of model execution

title: Data Center Technician, Data Center Operations
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 13, 2026

The Infrastructure Operations team is looking for cleared Data Center Technicians to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team. Data Center Technicians are the primary resolver and troubleshoot and solve a range of datacenter infrastructure issues including, but not limited to: hardware, fiber, networking, and related problems.

If you like to use IT principles like computer architecture and the OSI model (Open Systems Interconnection Model) and apply them to finding solutions to problems, we’d like to meet you. Your work will help to maintain one of the world's largest information system infrastructures.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities
You will be required to engage in physical data center activities with or without reasonable accommodation. This includes all tasks associated with planning and tracking capacity, rack deployment, rack cabling, hardware and software troubleshooting, and rack decommissioning. These activities include the following:
- Lifting and moving material up to 49 pounds each
- Working in cramped and/or elevated locations
- Bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching
- Standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
- Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation
- Work in a noisy environment
- Work shifts longer than 8 hours to support 24/7 operations (covering both night and day shifts).


A day in the life
Our Data Center Technician professionals, who have industry-leading technical abilities and demonstrate a breadth of knowledge:

- Show a strong aptitude for troubleshooting and problem solving
- Solve problems at their root and step back to understand the broader context
- Maintain service level agreements through the implementation of proactive issue detection and reporting
- Are biased to act in the absence of direction or support
- Improve effectiveness through process innovation

title: Manager I Ops, NOC Relay Ops
descriptionHtml:
Looking for a career at a company that seeks to be Earth’s most customer-centric company? If so, meet Amazon.

Over the past 20 years, Amazon has reinvented on behalf of customers and has become the largest internet retailer and marketplace in the world. Through our entrepreneurial culture, Amazon has developed new technologies and products (like Echo) and, enterprise services (like Amazon Web Services).
NOC (Network Operation Center) is the central command and control center for ‘Transportation Execution’ across the Amazon's transportation network. It ensures hassle free, timely pick-up and delivery of freight from vendors to Amazon fulfillment centers (FC) and from Amazon FCs to carrier hubs. In case of any exceptions, NOC steps in to resolve the issue and keeps all the stakeholders informed on the proceedings. Along with this tactical problem solving, NOC is also charged with understanding trends in network exceptions and then automating processes or proposing process changes to streamline operations. This second aspect involves network monitoring and significant analysis of network data.
Overall, NOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time.

Responsibilities of a NOC PM
We are looking for an experienced Program Manager to coordinate and lead efforts across operations, multiple technology and cross-border program teams. We're looking for a hands-on and motivated self-starter who's passionate about using data to help us measure every area of the business, drive efficiencies, optimizations and influence decision-making. This role is a part of the centralized Network Operations Centre (NOC) org part of Amazon India. This role is based in Dalian, China and will be required to work for Amazon Japan.
A Program Manager is expected to have deep functional knowledge, ability to design new program frameworks/processes and running defect reduction programs. They should be proficient, in identifying the input and output metric to gauge the success of a program. In this role, they will work with business and operations team to analyze historic results, challenge status quo and make business recommendations to senior management based on those analyses – all in an environment of rapid growth and increasing complexity. The Program Manager will drive improvements to the reporting tools, methods, and processes utilized by the team to increase the availability and granularity of actionable data to internal and external partners. The successful candidate must have very strong analytical skills and expert in excel. Knowledge of SQL and tools like R/Python would be an added advantage. They will be experienced at working with large data sets and the technical tools needed to work with them. They will have superb communication and customer-relationship skills, outstanding analytic insight, and be a passionate advocate of operations team to other stakeholders. They will drive towards simple, scalable solutions to difficult problems, have excellent project-management skills, and be able to communicate complex analytical results, both written and verbally, in a clear and easy-to-understand way. This candidate is also expected to handle small sized operations teams (3-10 L3) to design and publish relevant reports to track overall program progress.
The incumbent will own the following -
1) They will be responsible for working with supply chain execution, transportation, FC, carriers and other Amazon teams to identify pain points and scope out large high impact projects
2) They will be responsible for driving cost benefit analysis and go/no-go decisions on various initiatives
3) Once a go decision is made, the program manager will work to evolve a plan and timeline for execution.
4) The program manager will develop a roadmap and metrics to measure progress of the initiative they own. They will also own writing reports that detail the progress to leadership on a frequent basis
5) They will liaise across functions to drive their project and help clear issues and bottlenecks.
6) They will work with technology teams to scope out and drive any tech changes that are needed

Above all, we expect program managers to be single threaded owners for their initiatives.
Program Managers will be measured on the impact of their project. Depending on the project, clear financial or other impact goals will be set forth. It is the program manager's responsibility to ensure they drive the program towards achieving those goals.

What are we really looking for?
• You should be very analytical and be able to justify your decisions and approaches with data
• You should be able to deal with a high degree of ambiguity
• You should be able to take a complex problem and break it down to smaller digestible chunks
• You should be able to define a logical and step by step approach to achieving assigned goals
• You should be comfortable with processes and process design/analysis
• You should have the ability to influence without authority and do so by using data and facts
• You should be able to deal with varied stakeholders and earn their trust
• You are mature and able to function independently with limited guidance
• You should be willing to travel 30% of the time
• Languages proficiency (mandatory) – Japanese.

As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. - Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Do you like to use network and Unix systems engineering to deliver simple, sustainable, and repeatable solutions? Would you like to play a key role in driving the stability and sustainability of next-generation IP networks?

The Networking team is looking for an Optical Network Development Engineer to join our team. As an Optical Network Development Engineer, you will be responsible for building, deploying and scaling the Amazon networks that support AWS, customers, and other business units, across multiple global data centers.

AWS Core Networking is focused on building Data Centers and the network that allows Data Centers to function efficiently. They own the solutions that allow racks to be aggregated and Data Centers to be interconnected. Core Networking’s goal is to balance efficiency, performance and reliability to allow customers access to their applications and data.

Key job responsibilities
Optical Network Development Engineers perform high quality network and/or systems operations, deployments, scaling, technology refresh, sustaining engineering, best practices application, optimization, internal/external customer interactions, and produce appropriate technical documentation.

• Collaborate with vendors/manufacturers to evaluate new hardware and software features. Create implementations plans for incorporating them into the network.
• Automate optical test plans and qualify optical modules.
• Collaborate with vendors/manufactures in defining and developing test plans for Optical Modules.
• Create processes that help operate and build our DWDM network. Drive scaling current DWDM designs to meet the demand of our customers.
• Drive operational excellence projects to deliver improvements in our DWDM network quality and reliability.

A day in the life
Engineers in the InterDC Optical services team have a wide range of responsibilities. In terms of product development and delivery, it covers all activities related to hardware and software development, cross-platforms and software integration, and transition to production for both inhouse commodity and OEM optical platforms. From the lifecycle support perspective, includes day to day operations on-call, sustaining engineering, operational load automation and reduction, product and network security, network data integrity and authoritativeness, availability assurance (SRLG monitoring) and improvement (OLP, RFTS) and fiber infrastructure and vendor performance management.

Our engineers not only make decisions on day-to-day work but they also own the long-term strategic view, they build strong partnership with customers to understand their immediate and future needs, their use cases and the things that we/they are not even thinking about so we make sure our solutions will fit into their needs. They bring perspective and context to influence the way we make technology and design choices, how we develop and deliver products that are right sized, fungible and future proof at the optimum cost per bit. They understand the business impact of their recommendations and show good judgment in decision making as we consider technical trade-offs between the immediate short-term technology solutions, operational needs and the long-term business needs.

The InterDC Optical Services team is responsible for the development, delivery and lifecycle support of the optical products used to interconnect AWS Data Centers and PoPs (Point of presence), ensuring diversity of supply and continually lowering data transfer cost for customers. This product portfolio serves a broad customer base and is primarily used to transport Core (EC2 & Prod) and Border (Internet) traffic in and across all but a few AWS commercial and ADC regions globally. Our current network size is >10Pbps of inter data center traffic over >30k devices worldwide and our team is structured to create and evolve these products and solutions while providing highly available, secure and scalable transport for multiple customer fabrics globally.

title: Sr. Network Development Engineer, Satellite Systems Integration and Test, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of satellites in Low Earth Orbit. Its mission is to provide fast, reliable, and affordable connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.

The Satellite Systems Integration and Test team validates the complete communications path across the satellite payload, ground gateways, customer terminals, transport networks, and cloud services. We integrate new capabilities, evaluate end-to-end performance, troubleshoot complex failures, and reproduce issues observed during satellite operations.

As a Senior Network Development Engineer, you will lead hands-on integration and testing of satellite communications and ground-network capabilities. You will work across RF, networking, wireless protocols, embedded software, cloud services, and test automation to bring new features from initial lab integration through end-to-end validation.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys working directly with complex systems, collecting evidence, analyzing packet captures and logs, understanding RF link behavior, and driving ambiguous problems to root cause. You will collaborate with systems, hardware, software, RF, networking, and operations teams to determine whether failures originate in the satellite payload, RF link, gateway, customer terminal, transport network, or cloud service.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead end-to-end integration and validation of satellite communications features across the satellite payload, ground gateways, customer terminals, transport networks, and cloud services.
• Develop and execute test campaigns covering functionality, performance, reliability, scale, and failure recovery.
• Translate system and product requirements into test plans, use cases, success criteria, and verification matrices.
• Bring up new test configurations by integrating customer terminals, gateway equipment, satellite payload systems, RF equipment, network infrastructure, and cloud services.
• Troubleshoot complex system issues using packet captures, system logs, telemetry, performance counters, RF measurements, and test data.
• Use tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, iperf, and Linux networking utilities to isolate packet loss, latency, session failures, and throughput degradation.
• Analyze behavior across the communications stack, including RF link conditions, MAC behavior, Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking, transport protocols, and application performance.
• Troubleshoot packet loss and performance degradation caused by retransmissions, congestion, MTU issues, routing behavior, link conditions, and TCP or UDP behavior.
• Correlate RF conditions such as signal level, interference, link margin, channel impairments, and modulation performance with network and application behavior.
• Reproduce functional and performance issues observed during satellite operations in a controlled lab environment.
• Work with RF and test-equipment vendors to expand lab capabilities using spectrum analyzers, channel emulators, vector signal generators and analyzers, and customer-terminal simulators.
• Automate test execution, data collection, log processing, performance analysis, and reporting using Python or similar languages.
• Communicate technical findings clearly and drive cross-functional teams toward root cause, corrective action, and verification.
• Create and maintain test procedures, verification matrices, test records, dashboards, troubleshooting guides, and program-level status reports.
• Mentor engineers and establish repeatable integration, troubleshooting, and validation practices across the team.


Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or
national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the
U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent work experience
- 10+ years of experience in either satellite communications, cellular systems, wireless systems, modem validation, network integration, or end-to-end communications testing.
- Experience troubleshooting complex systems using packet captures, system logs, performance counters, and telemetry.
- Experience with Linux and network troubleshooting tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, ping, traceroute, iperf, and standard Linux networking utilities.
- Knowledge of IP networking, including TCP and UDP behavior, routing, VLANs, IP addressing, MTU, packet loss, latency, and throughput analysis.
- Experience integrating and testing systems that combine hardware, software, networking, RF components, and external test equipment.
- Experience developing test automation or data-analysis tools using Python or a similar programming language.
- Experience leading technical investigations across multiple engineering teams and communicating complex findings.

Preferred qualifications

- • Master’s or PhD degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, telecommunications, or a related discipline.
- • Experience with satellite payloads, satellite ground systems, gateways, customer terminals, or over-the-air communications testing.
- • Experience with cellular systems and 3GPP protocols, including LTE, 5G NR, Layer 2 and Layer 3 procedures, mobility, and performance testing.
- • Understanding of RF link behavior and its effect on network performance, including link margin, fading, interference, modulation, coding, and retransmissions.
- Experience with RF test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, vector signal generators and analyzers, channel emulators, power meters, and terminal simulators.
- Experience troubleshooting modem or wireless protocol-stack behavior from the MAC layer through the application layer.
- Experience with TCP congestion behavior, UDP loss, Quality of Service, routing, traffic generation, and network-performance analysis.
- Experience querying and visualizing test data using SQL, Grafana, or similar tools.
- Experience with AWS services, cloud networking, software-defined networking, or network automation.
- Experience taking wireless or communications features from initial integration through system validation and production deployment.
- Strong technical leadership, documentation, and cross-functional coordination skills.

To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Do you want to build the agentic platform that millions of administrators rely on to run their cloud desktops? The AWS WorkSpaces Forefront team is reinventing how customers discover onboard and manage WorkSpaces by embedding generative AI directly into our consoles and SDK. As a Senior Software Development Engineer you will be a key contributor to our agentic harness - the always-on platform layer that hosts our LLM agents: the agent loop and orchestration routing across a mixture of specialized experts personalization and memory tool/function calling over MCP retrieval and - a major area of focus for this role - the ranking and evaluation systems that decide what each agent surfaces and prove it's getting better over time. This is the shared substrate that powers AI experiences across multiple WorkSpaces products and you'll help shape and scale it alongside a team of strong engineers.

We are a fungible mix of front-end back-end and ML/AI engineers driving higher customer conversion through AI-powered onboarding building a suite of AI capabilities into our consoles - LLM agents personalization recommendations and experimentation - and unifying our platform at the architectural level. The harness is where these come together: a mixture-of-experts agent platform on Amazon Bedrock (AgentCore/Strands) MCP servers that give agents persistent working memory and typed access to backend services a RAG-backed knowledge base for conversational Q&A ranking and relevance layers that order recommendations and retrieved context and offline/online evaluation harnesses that measure agent quality and gate every change.

At Amazon we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. As a Senior SDE you'll lead the design and delivery of major components of the harness - with a particular emphasis on ranking and evaluation - tackle ambiguous greenfield problems where no playbook exists and raise the engineering bar across the team through design review mentorship and operational excellence. Because the harness is a multi-product platform you'll partner closely with other engineers UX and applied science across products - your work shows up in customer conversion admin productivity and the velocity of every team building on the platform.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead the ranking and evaluation systems for the harness - relevance and ranking of recommendations and retrieved context and the offline/online evaluation harnesses (golden datasets LLM-as-judge regression and drift detection human-in-the-loop feedback) that measure agent quality and gate changes before they reach customers. -Design the metrics and experimentation that turn agent quality into decision-grade signal (task completion recommendation acceptance conversion) and close the loop from production feedback back into ranking and model/prompt improvements. -Lead the design and delivery of other major harness components - the agent loop orchestration intent routing session and memory tool/function calling or streaming - and contribute significantly to its multi-quarter technical roadmap. -Help define the platform contracts (MCP tool interfaces identity pass-through agent-to-service seams) that let specialized expert agents and product teams build on the harness safely and independently. -Design and scale parts of a mixture-of-experts agent architecture on Amazon Bedrock (AgentCore/Strands) that is low-cost to train and serve with clear patterns for adding new domains. -Contribute to safety and relevance guardrails and the production quality/safety bar alongside the evaluation systems above. -Build highly scalable low-latency fault-tolerant distributed systems and share in operational excellence for the harness (latency availability cost on-call readiness). -Raise the technical bar across the team: participate in and lead design reviews mentor SDEs and influence direction with UX applied science and partner teams across products.

A day in the life
You might spend the morning extending the evaluation harness with new golden cases and a regression gate for the recommendation agent pair with an applied scientist at midday to tune the ranking layer and read out an A/B result and in the afternoon shape the MCP contract for a new expert agent - then write the one-pager that aligns the teams building on it. You'll operate in an agile environment where development cycles are measured in weeks take on the hardest and most ambiguous parts of the platform and be one of the technical leaders the team turns to when the answer isn't obvious. WorkSpaces Forefront owns the admin experience across the WorkSpaces Consoles (Personal Applications) and the WorkSpaces SDK. We're building an agentic control plane for Console and programmatic experiences - an agentic harness (LLM agents routing ranking personalization memory knowledge bases MCP tools and evaluation) plus experimentation and closed-loop learning - while unifying key infrastructure toward a federated console architecture.

title: Instock Manager, Amazon Pharmacy
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon Pharmacy's Supply Chain team and help shape how medications reach patients. Amazon Pharmacy is looking for an experienced Instock Manager with proven experience managing complex inbound supply chains in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment. You will join a high-powered, collaborative team where you partner across multiple functions to keep patients supplied with the medications they depend on.

Pharmacy is one of the most meaningful and interesting supply chains you can work on. Every in-stock decision you make helps ensure a patient gets the medication they're counting on, so your work has a direct, tangible impact on people's health. It's also a rich problem space: you'll navigate product expiry, controlled-substance handling, and state-by-state regulations, solving challenges that don't exist in traditional retail. If you want the ownership of an instock role plus a mission that matters, this is a rare place to build.

The Instock Manager will be responsible for all aspects of the Instock role, including driving improved in-stock, inventory planning, and vendor operational improvement (efficiency, fill rates, lead times). You will drive initiatives to improve patient experience, reduce cost, and improve inventory health by working collaboratively across pharmacy operations, supply chain, procurement, and compliance teams. The ideal candidate excels in scalable process improvement, automation, and analytics, and is energized by solving complex problems and turning manual processes into scalable ones.

Strong written and verbal communication skills are required, and the candidate should be comfortable engaging with both internal stakeholders and vendors. The candidate will have proven experience delivering results by partnering with others and be comfortable contributing across a range of topics outside the core ISM responsibilities.

Key job responsibilities
Maintain excellent in-stock rates for owned category and/or region while minimizing expiry and unhealthy inventory
Execute inventory strategies to optimize service levels, turns, and inventory health under expiry and controlled-substance constraints
Monitor, analyze, and own key performance indicators such as in-stock rate, target inventory levels, fill rate, turns, and expiry/write-off rates
Manage efficient inbound and outbound inventory flows and health, including supporting purchasing processes and removing unproductive or expiring inventory in a compliant manner
Drive root cause analysis and reporting on operational issues, develop action plans, and project manage improvements while managing multiple competing priorities simultaneously
Partner with vendor managers to drive vendor performance across fill rate, lead time, and reliability
Work collaboratively with internal teams to drive tools and process improvements affecting purchasing and procurement workflows, with emphasis on automating tasks currently performed manually
Ensure inventory and procurement decisions adhere to pharmacy regulatory and compliance requirements across states

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of supply chain, inventory management or project management experience
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience using strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills
- Experience with SQL and advanced Excel
- Ability to thrive in a high energy environment where tactical and strategic activities are expected to be driven in parallel

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field
- Track record of delivering results and an ability to operate both strategically and tactically in a high-energy, fast-paced environment
- Strong numerical and analytical aptitude, and high proficiency creating and managing advanced models

title: Program Manager, Instore Experience (ISX), Reverse Logistic Services (RLS)
descriptionHtml:
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) exists to make returns effortless and reliable for every Amazon customer — no matter which store or partner they walk into. In France, we deliver that experience across more than 15,000 partner and carrier locations, through convenience-led options such as Label-Free, Box-Free (LFBF) drop-off and every other way a customer can return an item in-store.

The ISX Regional Program Manager, France owns the quality and consistency of that experience across the whole French network. Because returns run through thousands of independent partner sites, the experience can vary widely from one location to the next and the core of this role is closing that gap. You will get into the field, see how returns actually happen at partner locations, coach partners and their teams to the standard customers expect, and use data to focus your time on the sites that need help most. Your mission is holistic: improving in-store returns execution across all return types, so a customer's experience is just as good at the busiest location as it is at the smallest.

This is not only a field-execution role. It carries a strategic remit that reflects its level. Beyond coaching individual sites, you will help design and deploy the network-wide improvements that lift the entire France network at once: in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment mechanisms, associate support and training, and the tools partners rely on to process returns. You will translate what you learn in the field into scalable programs, work across internal teams to launch them in France, and help shape how the broader EU standards themselves are built, turning local, on-the-ground insight into lasting structural improvement.

This is also a founding, build-from-scratch role. You'll be the first ISX Program Manager for France and one of the earliest members of the EU field team, reporting directly to the EU ISX Senior Manager. There's no established playbook yet, you'll help create it. We're looking for someone with real ambition, comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to focus relentlessly on the initiatives that matter most while the team, tools, and standards are still taking shape.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the in-store returns experience in France across ~17,000 partner and carrier locations, ensuring returns are fast, easy, and reliable for customers across all return types.
• Get into the field and coach. Visit partner locations, observe how returns are handled, and coach partner teams to Amazon's standards for speed, accuracy, and customer experience.
• Use data to prioritize. You can't be everywhere. Use performance data to identify the locations and partners falling furthest behind and concentrate your effort where it improves the customer experience most.
• Drive measurable improvement on the metrics that define a great returns experience: how fast customers are served, how reliably returns are processed, customer satisfaction, and site readiness.
• Deploy network-wide improvements. Lead the rollout of scalable programs that raise the standard across the entire Italian network, including in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment, associate support and training, and returns-processing tools , using your field insight to prioritize and adapt them for the market.
• Shape strategy from the field. Turn on-the-ground observations into recommendations that influence how EU-wide returns standards, mechanisms, and programs are designed, ensuring the field perspective is built in from the start.
• Manage performance to resolution. Follow a structured coaching and follow-up cycle for underperforming sites, and partner with the right internal teams (Business Partnerships for retail partners, the Transportation team for carriers) when issues need to be escalated to a partner's leadership.
• Build the foundation. As a founding team member, help shape how the EU field team audits, coaches, and reports, adapting proven practices from the North America team to the French market and feed your field insights into the monthly ISX reporting that informs strategy.


A day in the life
You start the week by reviewing performance data for France and identifying the partner locations and carriers falling furthest behind on the customer experience. You spend time in the field visiting a risk-weighted set of those sites, watching real customers complete returns, checking that the process is running smoothly, and coaching partner teams on the spot. Back at your desk, you're also driving the French rollout of a new signage standard and a store-supplies replenishment mechanism, using what you saw in the field to shape how they're deployed. You log your findings, build improvement plans for the sites that need them, escalate the bigger systemic issues to the right internal team, and close the week by capturing insights for the monthly ISX report and re-planning around wherever the customer experience needs you most.

About the team
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) owns the returns journey end-to-end for Amazon, everything that happens after a customer decides to send something back until delivery at our FC. Our purpose is simple but hard: make returns effortless and reliable for every customer, while running one of the largest, most complex reverse-logistics networks in retail.

Within RLS, the In-Store Experience (ISX) team focuses on where returns meet the real world, the thousands of partner and carrier locations customers walk into to drop off an item. We turn a single promise into a consistent reality across every one of them: fast, easy, dependable returns, no matter which door a customer chooses. Working from the field, we close the gap between the best and worst locations, coach partners to a standard customers can count on, and build the mechanisms that lift the whole network at once.

Our culture is hands-on, data-driven, and high-ownership. We obsess over the customer, thrive in ambiguity, dive deep into the details on the ground, and think big about how to scale what works — because the best decisions about in-store returns are made by people who've seen them happen firsthand.

descriptionHtml:
AWS is seeking a Senior Customer Success Specialist - AI Driven Digital Product Delivery to lead strategic transformation initiatives for organizations adopting Amazon Kiro and AWS's generative AI platform to revolutionize how they build and deliver digital products. This is a senior individual contributor role within the AWS Specialists & Partners (ASP) Customer Success Center of Excellence, requiring a combination of executive-level strategic vision and practical credibility to help customers fundamentally reimagine their software development lifecycle using AI.

Amazon Kiro is AWS's AI-powered platform that transforms how organizations build software, from requirements gathering and architecture design to code generation, testing, and deployment. This role focuses on helping customers move beyond AI-assisted coding to systematic AI-driven digital product delivery transformation at enterprise scale.
You will define the methodologies, frameworks, and repeatable models that shape how AWS and its customers approach AI-driven digital product delivery transformation. Your work will directly influence product roadmaps, partner ecosystems, and go-to-market strategies, creating lasting organizational and market impact across hundreds of organizations globally.

descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s Deployment Safety team and build the intelligent systems that keep our most critical cloud infrastructure running flawlessly. As a Software Development Engineer II, you’ll use AI and automation to design, test, and deploy updates for EC2 Frontier with precision and scale. You’ll own every stage of the development lifecycle—from crafting AI-enhanced deployment pipelines that predict risks to creating automated testing tools that catch defects before they reach production. By integrating machine learning models to analyze deployment data and real-time monitoring to flag anomalies, you’ll help millions of Amazon customers rely on infrastructure that’s safer, faster, and more resilient.

This role is for collaborative engineers who thrive on solving ambiguous problems, mentoring peers, and turning cutting-edge AI concepts into practical, high-impact solutions. If you’re passionate about blending cloud-native engineering with intelligent automation, we want to hear from you.

#AI #MachineLearning #DeploymentSafety #Cloud #Frontier

Key job responsibilities
• Collaborate with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to conceive, design, and bring innovative products and services to market.
• Design and build innovative technologies in a large distributed computing environment and help lead fundamental changes in the industry.
• Create solutions to run predictions on distributed systems with exposure to innovative technologies at incredible scale and speed.
• Build distributed storage, index, and query systems that are scalable, fault-tolerant, low cost, and easy to manage/use.

A day in the life
Your morning begins with a collaborative code review—leveraging AI-assisted tools to provide feedback that elevates the team’s code quality and readiness for deployment. You pair with a teammate to tackle a tricky integration point, using real-time debugging tools to ensure seamless automation.

Then, you investigate an operational metric that’s flagged by your anomaly detection system, tracing it to a root cause using ML-powered correlation engines. Within hours, you’ve drafted a fix that not only resolves the issue but also enhances your predictive safety models.

Your day balances deep, heads-down coding on cloud-native features with cross-functional problem-solving—all while driving operational excellence and mentoring peers. Every task you tackle reinforces our mission: building smarter, safer systems that millions of Amazon customers rely on daily.

descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!
About the Role:

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement.

You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations.

You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals.

• You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells.

• You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components.

• You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc.

- Experience troubleshooting and repairing operational items
- Knowledge of mathematics
- Experience measurement reading and interpretation
- Work flexible schedules including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

descriptionHtml:

The Frontier ADC team is at the forefront of delivering the AWS GenAI and Agentic AI service portfolio to our customers in GovCloud and isolated environments. We are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what is possible in this rapidly evolving field, leveraging the power of cloud computing and the latest advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies. With a focus on expanding Frontier AI services across GovCloud and isolated regions, driving automation investments, and delivering innovative solutions, we are at the forefront of modernization. Our teams are innovating new ways of building massively scalable distributed systems and delivering the next generation of cloud computing across the GenAI and Agentic AI service portfolio. We are seeking a Systems Development Engineer II who can think big and simplify solutions to complex problems, all while ensuring our customers continue to have the best experience possible!

A successful Systems Development Engineer II joining the team will be an innovator, building solutions and working closely with Amazon's largest and most demanding government customers to address their specific needs across a suite of Frontier AI services in GovCloud and isolated environments. They will drive the resolution of technical issues and work diligently to improve the customer experience.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

The ideal candidate will:

• Be great fun to work with. Our company credo is "Work hard. Have fun. Make history". The right candidate will love what they do and instinctively know how to make work fun.

descriptionHtml:
What happens when you combine startup speed with Amazon-scale impact? You get this team. Amazon Enterprise Security Products is a newly launched group building intelligent, cloud-agnostic security tools using AI-first development practices. Here, you build AI and you build with AI — at the same time. This is not a traditional SDE role. It's a chance to shape the future of security tooling with a small, fast team that ships like a startup and deploys like Amazon.

Key job responsibilities
* Design, build, and ship AI-powered security products: Own the full lifecycle from architecture through production deployment of large-scale, multi-tiered distributed systems that protect AWS Customers. Leverage agentic AI development practices to accelerate every phase.

* Engineer end-to-end, full-stack experiences: Build across the entire stack with intuitive front-end interfaces, robust back-end services and REST APIs, and intelligent middleware. Deploy on AWS while designing for cloud-agnostic, multi-cloud environments so customers are protected wherever they operate.

* What you build: Design and implement the intelligent systems customers interact with — agentic architectures, conversational interfaces, and automation workflows that make AI-first security real at scale.
* How you build: Use AI tools and techniques (established and experimental) to write, test, review, and ship code faster. Multiplying your own velocity, quality, and creative output across greenfield and brownfield projects.

* Plan, estimate, and drive delivery: Lead implementation planning, effort estimation, and phased rollouts across systems and operations; you own outcomes with the autonomy and accountability expected in a high-trust startup environment.

* Prototype rapidly and innovate relentlessly: Validate hypotheses with customers, iterate quickly, and bring a builder's mindset every day. The best idea wins here regardless of where it comes from.

* Partner across disciplines: Work directly with security researchers, applied scientists, product managers, and UX designers to shape product direction and turn customer needs into technical solutions. Small team means short lines between you and the decision.

* Own operational excellence: Participate in on-call rotations, drive root-cause analysis, and continuously raise the bar on reliability, performance, and security of the systems you build. You ship it, you run it..

* Elevate the team — and yourself: Contribute to technical reviews, mentor teammates, and champion AI-first development practices. You'll build the engineering culture of a fast-growing team from the ground floor, and in the process become the kind of engineer who has shaped a product, scaled an organization, and defined how modern security software gets built.

A day in the life
No two days look the same on this fast growing, AI first development team. You might start your morning reviewing output from overnight agentic coding sessions, then dive into building a RAG pipeline or designing APIs that connect intelligent interfaces to real time threat data across multiple clouds. After lunch, you join a design session with senior and principal engineers where your ideas carry weight regardless of title. You own features end to end, ship using the latest AI assisted development workflows, and see your work reach production fast. This is where builders thrive.

About the team
Amazon Enterprise Security Products is built by builders who tackle challenges others might consider too ambitious. We're a small team where there are no layers between you and the decision, no waiting quarters to see your work reach customers. Every team member brings an owner's mentality. If there's a problem worth solving, we solve it. No mission is beyond reach, no detail beneath our attention. We move fast, we ship fast, and we learn from what we ship. This is where builders who want to make the impossible routine come to do their best work.

Diverse Experiences

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Air Quality Engineer, AWS Environmental
descriptionHtml:
As an Air Quality Engineer you will play a key role in air permitting and air quality compliance for new and existing AWS facilities in the Americas (AMER) region. You will be the environmental representative on behalf of the AWS Environmental Team in AMER responsible for the successful delivery of air permitting projects. You will partner with stakeholders across AWS to develop standards and mechanisms that incorporate air quality permitting into the process of planning, building, and operating data centers. You will manage strategic air quality engineering and air permitting projects and provide regulatory compliance guidance for both design and operations teams. The Air Quality Engineer will also work with internal and external partners that include government entities, AWS regional environmental engineers, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders. You will regularly engage with stakeholders; report to AWS Environmental leaders; and ensure risks to air permitting and compliance pathways are being appropriately identified, communicated, and managed.

The successful candidate will have a strong track record of air quality engineering solutions and air permitting in North America, the demonstrated ability to deliver multiple high priority projects simultaneously, the ability to drive alignment across teams with competing priorities, and be a strong advocate for air quality compliance and sustainability.

Key job responsibilities
• Function as a leader for air permitting work in AMER by managing the preparation of air permit applications for new construction, modifications, amendments, and renewals.
• Manage contracts and relationships with environmental consultants and testing firms to complete air permit applications and air dispersion modeling analyses.
• Manage regulatory agency interactions for permit evaluation and processing, and new process and technology introduction.
• Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently.
• Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company.
• Review environmental permitting requirements for new power generation technologies, including both prime power generation and back up emergency power for data centers.
• Work collaboratively with energy, design engineering, public policy, capacity delivery, real estate, due diligence, and legal teams on large scale projects with undefined scope and drive towards sustainable long term energy supply solutions.

A day in the life
This role's primary focus is to function as an environmental air quality engineering leader and implement centralized management systems that support AWS growth and compliance in the Americas. You will work directly with partner teams throughout the data center development lifecycle to encourage sustainable air quality development and design and to ensure compliance with local, state and federal air regulations. Beyond the day-to-day responsibilities, you will monitor and review evolving and emerging air quality permitting/modeling regulations; you may be required to assess impact(s) of regulatory changes to AWS and propose course of action.

The AWS Environmental team is a dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The Environmental team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.
