title: Manager, Account Management, NA AVS
descriptionHtml:
About Amazon.com
Amazon.com strives to be Earth's most customer-centric company where people can find and discover virtually anything they want to buy online. By giving customers more of what they want - low prices, vast selection, and convenience - Amazon.com continues to grow and evolve as a world-class e-commerce platform. Amazon's evolution from Web site to e-commerce partner to development platform is driven by the spirit of innovation that is part of the company's DNA. The world's brightest technology minds come to Amazon.com to research and develop technology that improves the lives of shoppers and sellers around the world.
About the Role
Team Manager, Account Management, North America (NA), Work Timings: 3pm-12am IST
As a Manager, Account Management as part of Amazon Vendor Services (AVS) NA Team of Retail Business Services, you will have the exciting opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy for managing Amazon AVS North America vendors.
AVS team is looking for a bright, customer centric, driven, and creative people leader to join our team. The role leads a team of Account Managers responsible for managing business growth for some of the most influential Selling Partners (vendors) on Amazon, ensuring Selling Partner satisfaction with the program through a high level of service and operational standards. In this role, you will manage strategic joint business plans for Selling Partners across your team by collaborating with them to explore innovative ways to identify and execute new selection, merchandising, and operational improvement opportunities. You will interface internally with leaders from our Retail and Vendor Services teams and will be responsible for all aspects of the vendor’s business with Amazon. Your team will engage directly with multiple internal teams to optimize the product line for key manufacturers (vendors) on Amazon. The candidate thrives in an ambiguous environment where they must develop, implement and iterate data, processes, mechanisms and guardrails to improve the customer experience. Further, the candidate is a business owner who understands the key levers to drive business growth and can operationalize those levers across their team. They have a passion for people leadership and are at their best when they’re building, developing and managing high-performing teams. Your team will utilize a wide range of skills and work across major functional areas such as site merchandising, buying, inventory management, finance, operations and online marketing, to drive the performance of strategic vendor partners at Amazon. In this role you will be focused on the strategic and operational aspects of managing the customer relationships with our vendors.
You will lead the team to conceive, create and analyze a wide range of marketing and site merchandising efforts, to include marketing campaigns to grow the vendor’s traffic, brand awareness, customer conversion, and revenue on Amazon. Also you will look into strategic and operational aspects of their business with Amazon, root cause analysis of issues and opportunities affecting the vendor’s business.

Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities Include
· Lead a team of Account Managers, prioritizing strategic initiatives and provide escalation support as needed.
· Success will be measured by the performance of your internal teams on input metrics and impact of vendors on creating a great customer experience for buying consumers
· Identify, action and/or provide advice on how to improve business input metrics that drive growth and improve end customer experience, in collaboration with other Amazon programs and teams.
· Manage end to end goal setting for team to align with organizational goals.
· Build relationships with Selling Partners across the portfolio; proactively build joint business plan action items and act as a point of escalation for issues, questions, and concerns.
· Act as a thought leader in defining success criteria and understand business needs of Selling Partners in an ever-changing business environment. Contributes to and leads strategic plans and documents for the organization.
· Leads recruiting and hiring efforts across direct team and broader organization.
· Manage Selling Partner needs and monitor complexity through efficient resource allocation of Account Managers.
· Monitor Selling Partner satisfaction survey results to analyze both positive and negative feedback trends. Establish improvement plans and mange expectations with Account Managers as appropriate.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 3+ years of team management experience
- Experience analyzing data and best practices to assess performance drivers
- Experience influencing internal and external stakeholders
- Experience with sales CRM tools such as Salesforce or similar software

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of mentoring, leading and coaching experience

descriptionHtml:

The TAM works with customers as a trusted advisor to enable their cloud journey and grow their knowledge of AWS cloud services and technologies to support their business goals.

As we continue to rapidly expand AWS’s Enterprise Support organization you’ll have plenty of opportunities to develop your technical, consulting, operational and leadership skills. This role is within our Strategic Industries group, and specifically within the team looking after strategic accounts in the Energy and Utilities vertical.

title: Senior Account Manager, Quick Commerce, Last Mile Logistics, Delivery Service Partners (Saudi National)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Delivery Service Partners are business owners who build and run last mile delivery businesses for Amazon. As a Senior Account Manager, you will be their advisor and operating partner. You will lead a team of 6+ managers who look after 80+ delivery partners in Amazon’s quick commerce business (15 minute and 2 hour delivery) across Saudi Arabia. Some owners are first-time entrepreneurs with no logistics background, and others are seasoned logistics carriers.

You will manage each partner relationship across the whole lifecycle of the business. That means helping owners solve their biggest challenges, shaping their business planning, and spotting obstacles early so they can make sound decisions and succeed.

This role requires flexibility and regular travel between sites to meet business owners in person every week.

Key job responsibilities
As a Logistics Account Manager, you will manage a team of 6+ Managers to manage 80+ DSP accounts in Amazon's quick commerce business (15min and 2H delivery) across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia including entrepreneurs with no background in the logistics industry, or seasoned logistics carrier (Depending on business program)

Work closely with a portfolio of owners at different stages as they set strategy, help drive accountability and engagement, and motivate and track key performance metrics.

Collaborate with an integrated internal team of Program Managers and Compliance and Finance personnel to ensure owners launch and scale their business in compliance with program requirements.

Support owners by removing obstacles and improving financial, operational, and safety practices at the network level.

As Lead, Logistics Supply chain Manager will do this by analyzing problems, discovering insights, delivering recommendations, and driving change both internally and externally.

They will collaborate frequently with a wide array of integrated internal stakeholders such as Partner Relations (PAR), Value Added Service (VAS), Legal, fleet and network health to name a few. The Logistics Supply chain Manager support owners by removing obstacles and improving financial, operational, and safety practices at the network level. They facilitate and execute Monitoring and Enforcement Policies (MEP) and build two-way feedback channels with OTR teams, DSPs and WW/EU Product and strategy.

The Logistics Supply chain Manager will be required to work flexibly and will be required to travel between multiple sites to engage with business owners weekly to carry out their role effectively.

A day in the life
- Lead your team and portfolio: Manage 6+ account managers and the 80+ delivery partners they support, helping owners set strategy, stay accountable, and track key performance metrics.
- Safety and compliance: Work with Amazon’s safety and regional operations teams to keep every partner business safe and compliant. Coach owners to run safe, compliant, high performing companies.
- Launch and scale: Support new owners through onboarding and launch (net new launches only). Guide owners as they scale, handle operational issues, and prepare ramp plans and driver supply for peak periods.
- Performance: Dig into customer metrics to find improvement opportunities, and coach owners to use Amazon’s delivery tools effectively.
- Process improvement: Find workflow inefficiencies and drive network level improvements that make life easier for owners. Push back on delivery station processes that hurt operations.
- Partner experience: Strengthen the relationship between Amazon and its delivery partners and improve their satisfaction. Raise driver standards to protect Amazon’s brand. Act as the voice of the delivery partners inside Amazon.
- Enforcement and feedback: Apply Amazon’s monitoring and enforcement policies, and build two-way feedback channels between operations teams, delivery partners, and global product and strategy teams.
- Cross-functional work: Partner with program management, compliance, finance, legal, fleet, network health, Partner Relations, and Value Added Services teams to help owners launch and grow within program requirements.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience influencing internal and external stakeholders
- 5+ years of team management experience

Preferred qualifications

- MBA
- 7+ years of account or relationship management, small business logistics, or retail/vendor/supplier management experience
- Bachelor's degree in management, business administration, economics, engineering, marketing
- Experience in transportation or supply chain

title: Business Analyst, Network Strategy & Performance, Network Strategy and Preformance
descriptionHtml:
Business Analyst in Network Strategy and Performance owns processes & analytics that directly shape how Amazon serves customers globally. They are an analytical problem solver who is comfortable in a fast-paced, multi-tasked, high-energy environment. They are self-motivated, operating independently in an autonomous environment to deliver an exceptional customer experience with little to no guidance. They operationalize the long- and short-term staffing plans, working cross-functionally with site Operations, planning teams, training, finance, and others. They will contribute to the team's AI-driven transformation agenda by applying AI tools to increase the speed, quality, and scale of analytical outputs. They do not just report or fix defects, but think critically about why they happen, what surrounds them, and how to prevent them — combining analytical rigor with a proactive, anticipatory mindset.

Key job responsibilities
- Create and accurately maintain CSA shift schedules ensuring shifts are optimally planned to meet the sites short term forecast requirements and Service Levels (SL).
- Monitor actual staffing levels against planned staffing and take the relevant corrective actions as required improve SL.
- Effectively plan and monitor CSA adherence to assigned schedule, including productive and non-productive activities.
- Work closely with mid to senior-level leaders across core teams to identify and mitigate emerging risks and assists in creating mitigation plans for staffing corrections and SL recovery.
- Responsible for coordinating site-staffing needs including reporting and analysis of site headcount numbers as per staffing plan.
- Understanding and monitor symptoms of CSA burnout, detecting the metrics that can signal these symptoms and assist in implementing interventions to eliminate outlier experiences.
- Responsible to coordinate various cross-training, new-hires, and management of network and site-wide shift rotation processes as per business need.
- Create work schedules for associates, identifies and proactively resolves headcount deficiencies and overages.
- Investigate defects and operational anomalies to identify systemic drivers (system-related, behavioral, or shared responsibility), not just symptoms. Highlight and communicate metrics impacting the operation that could impact service levels, customer experience, and business process.
- Build and maintain validation checks, dashboards, and automated alerts to catch defects early — before they impact customers or operations.
- Independently apply AI tools (e.g., Amazon Q, generative AI assistants, AgentZ) to accelerate analytical workflows, identifying opportunities to improve speed and quality of outputs.
- Apply AI tools to develop automation for repetitive tasks within your workstream, demonstrating measurable productivity improvement.


About the team
The Network Strategy and Performance (NP) team defines and delivers the right human-assisted support to Amazon customers under demand and labor supply volatility, by optimizing the Amazon Customer Service (CS) network for customer experience, associate experience, and cost. We are responsible for: (1) planning customer support staffing; (2) preserving the customer experience when customers contact Customer Service; and (3) ensuring best costs for providing customer support.
We analyse historical data and anticipate potential business events to accurately predict the number of Customer Service Associates (CSAs) required for a given period. Our areas of expertise span forecasting, planning, optimization, data analytics, and reporting. We deliver our vision using operations research, data science, and program management — and we continue to challenge the status quo, invent and simplify, and deliver excellence for our customers.
The Network Performance team is on a transformation journey. We are building a future-ready team that combines analytical rigor with AI fluency, executive-level communication, and the ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries. We are seeking a Business Analyst to join this team and help shape how Amazon plans, staff, and optimizes its Customer Service network.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of program or project management experience
- 1+ years of supply chain experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a quantitative field (engineering, economics, math, and statistics), business or equivalent
- 4+ years of supply chain experience, or a MBA and 4+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- Experience using AI-assisted development tools in academic or professional settings
- Knowledge of advanced skills in Excel as well as any data visualization tools like Tableau or similar BI tools (familiarity with Tableau preferred)
- Experience defining requirements and using data and metrics to draw business insights
- Experience demonstrating strong analytical abilities and confidence in the use of data
- Experience communicating clearly and concisely with leadership, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in MS Access and SQL
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document

title: NW Deployment Build Lead , Infra - GND
descriptionHtml:
Job description
AWS is looking for a Network Deploy Technician to join our growing team within infrastructure operations. You will work with minimum supervision in a dynamic environment to drive the stability and sustainability of our next-generation networks and assist in the development of innovative ways to automate and scale our network.

The position's responsibilities include scaling support of several data center locations and day to day assistance with capacity management. You will work closely with internal customers and external vendors to facilitate smooth project execution as directed by Network Leadership and Technical Project Managers.

You will leverage your experience supporting large scale, enterprise class networks as well as network implementation and troubleshooting. As a Network Deploy Technician, you will work in a fast paced, collaborative environment with regular peer and customer interaction. In addition to providing management and support of AWS’ vast network infrastructure, Network Deploy Technicians establish and follow best practices and refine operational procedures.

All physical requirements are expected with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
• Ability to work in an environment that operates 24/7 with an ability to participate in primary responder rotation and provide after-hours support as needed
• Working in cramped and/or elevated and/or noisy environments
• Bending, lifting, stretching, reaching, standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
• Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
• Managing work and priorities through ticketing system and workflows to complete customer requests and projects
• Collaborating with various stakeholders to remove project obstacles
• Troubleshooting networking, routing and interconnectivity issues, including patch panels and patch cords
• Specifying Power and Cooling requirements and ensuring Hardware Racking/Stacking completed for new equipment
• Participating in the migration, basic configuration and rollout of new or upgraded hardware

Traveling within and outside of regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

A day in the life
Our team has three primary tasks:
1. Providing the first level networking devices to serve our customer racks entails various tasks (the name of the game is efficiency): You will track network rack intake and delivery; work with various onsite teams to request for rack space, power, and cooling for network racks. And then partner with network engineers to ensure all configurations are ready. You'll also be working on link and device troubleshooting within a certain Service-Level Agreement
2. There is also console builds (and room builds) that are really exciting. You'll be exposed to more teams whose goal is to provide more space and capacity for customer racks.
3. Work with ID-Scaling peers to build higher-level networking devices.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of computer hardware troubleshooting and repair experience
- 1+ years of computer networking experience
- High school or equivalent diploma

Preferred qualifications

- Experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure

Our teams design, launch, and operate these integrations with a wide range of partners, and each launch has to work securely and seamlessly across many different systems, regions, and customer needs.

title: Risk Specialist I, EAP
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP) team is responsible for ensuring that Amazon's global operation is the benchmark for environmental excellence across all similar industries. EAP transforms environmental regulatory compliance into a zero-defect process through simple, scalable, and sustainable solutions that protect the business, our communities, and the environment.

The Risk Specialist I drives regulated waste compliance across the 2-4 sites they support. This specialist executes the organization's environmental compliance plans at the site level, tracks waste compliance obligations to closure, and partners with site and operations teams to meet compliance milestones. They conduct site inspections, maintain hazardous waste accumulation and manifesting records, and surface gaps through regular program controls.

The ideal candidate brings working knowledge of regulated waste requirements, including RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules. They communicate technical compliance requirements clearly to site leaders, operations partners, and legal stakeholders, and use data to find gaps, prioritize fixes, and improve conformance across their sites.

This role requires sound independent judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to run the right mechanisms and manage competing priorities to meet compliance objectives in a dynamic, high-pace operations environment. If you are motivated by solving regulatory compliance problems in the field, this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the execution and delivery of regulated waste compliance projects and activities, including developing standard operating procedures, workflows, and inspection routines, to mitigate identified risks across the sites you support.
- Apply risk management methods such as waste compliance audits and site inspections to monitor compliance thresholds, test controls, and take corrective action when findings arise.
- Collaborate with site teams, compliance operations, and operations partners to understand business needs, clarify waste compliance requirements, and drive productive discussions that build consensus.
- Identify process improvement opportunities and work with process owners to improve conformance, reduce risk, and increase operational efficiency.
- Prepare clear and concise documentation, including status reports, audit results, metrics, and project communications, so the right information reaches the right audience at the right time.
- Travel expected up to 50% of the time.

A day in the life
Your morning might begin by reviewing incoming risk-related requests and prioritizing your project tasks. You will spend time conducting audits or risk assessments, updating documentation, and coordinating with compliance operations and partner teams. Throughout the day, you will track project milestones, resolve roadblocks, and communicate progress to stakeholders. You will also look for ways to streamline existing processes and ensure your risk area stays aligned with current regulations and team objectives.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to protecting Amazon's customers and business by proactively managing risk across a broad range of areas, from regulatory compliance to operational resilience. We work closely with legal, operations, and business partners to deliver practical risk solutions and build a strong culture of compliance. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and creative problem-solving, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where every team member can grow and make an impact.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) or related field
- 2+ years of experience in environmental compliance, regulated waste management, or workplace risk investigations
- Experience interpreting and applying environmental regulations (RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules)
- Experience collecting and analyzing data to identify compliance gaps and drive corrective actions

title: SNR Reliability Maintenance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
- Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
- Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
- Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
- Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
- Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network

A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Relevant experience in a technical leadership role
- Relevant experience working in both electrical and mechanical disciplines
- Relevant experience in automation or material handling equipment environments
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working in a multi-contractor and multi-site working environment
- Understanding of PLC based controls systems and statutory compliance requirements
- Experience using computerised maintenance management systems to plan proactive maintenance and record reactive tasks
- A degree preferably in a technical discipline or operations

title: Video Editor & Media Manager, Amazon Leo Marketing
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network, built to deliver fast, reliable broadband to people and places beyond the reach of existing networks. From families and small businesses to schools, hospitals, and entire communities, we’re working to connect the world in ways that weren’t possible before. We just created a new brand. Now comes the fun part.

We’ve spent years building the technology and creating the Amazon Leo brand from the ground up. Now we’re bringing it to life. And we’ve got some incredible ingredients to work with: rockets launching into space, satellites orbiting hundreds of miles above Earth, innovative technology, and, most importantly, the people and communities whose lives will change when they get connected. There’s no shortage of great stories to tell. We just need the right people to help us tell them.

We’re looking for a Social Video Editor who’s equal parts storyteller, craftsman, and creative problem solver. Someone who can find a great story in hours of raw footage, knows how to make people stop scrolling, and brings their own creative instincts to every project.

This is a dual role, split evenly between creating social-first video content and helping us build the Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems that power our creative team. You’ll work across consumer, business, and government audiences around the world, helping shape how Amazon Leo looks, feels, and tells stories. If you love great storytelling, obsess over the details, and get excited about building something new, we’d love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
• Create compelling, social-first video content for Amazon Leo, including influencer collaborations, branded content, product storytelling, behind-the-scenes videos, and short-form social campaigns.
• Edit and craft engaging stories through pacing, music, sound design, motion graphics, color correction, and creative finishing. Bring strong editorial instincts and attention to detail to every project.
• Bring the Amazon Leo brand to life through creative use of Aurora particles, Krypton Purple, typography, motion, and sound. Find fresh and unexpected ways to use these elements to tell stories that feel unmistakably Amazon Leo.
• Adapt creative content for different social platforms, audiences, and formats, balancing platform trends and best practices with a consistent brand identity.
• Collaborate with Creative Directors, Social, Marketing, and production partners to develop and execute engaging video content for consumer, business, and government audiences.
• Transform complex technology and technical subjects into accessible, entertaining stories. Find the human moments that make people care about what we’re building.
• Partner with Social and Marketing teams to understand content performance and identify opportunities to improve future creative work.
• Help develop, organize, and manage Amazon Leo’s Digital Asset Management (DAM) system, supporting a growing global library of video, photography, animation, audio, and finished creative assets.
• Maintain consistent media management practices, including metadata, tagging, naming conventions, folder structures, version control, and project archiving.
• Support efficient workflows for ingesting, organizing, reviewing, approving, distributing, and retrieving creative assets across internal teams and external production partners.
• Maintain accurate asset information, including usage rights, permissions, and licensing details, to support secure and appropriate content sharing.
• Identify opportunities to improve post-production and asset management workflows, including exploring AI-assisted creative tools, automation, and new technologies.
• Manage multiple editing and asset management projects simultaneously, balancing creative quality, organization, and deadlines.
• Make outrageously cool content.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a fresh batch of footage from a creator who’s been putting Amazon Leo to the test. You’ve got hours of material, a few great moments, and an opportunity to tell a story that people actually want to watch. You jump into the edit, find the hook, experiment with music and pacing, and start turning raw footage into something worth sharing.

Next, you’re working with our creative and social teams on a new campaign. We’ve built an entirely new visual identity, and now we get to play with it. Aurora particles that bring connectivity to life. Krypton Purple, inspired by the technology powering our satellites. Golden Hour, capturing the warmth of the best moments in our customers’ lives. A distinct motion language, typography, and sonic identity. These aren’t just brand guidelines. They’re creative tools for finding new ways to tell stories.

Maybe you’re using Aurora particles to visualize a connection traveling across the world. Maybe you’re taking footage from a customer documentary and turning it into a compelling 30-second social story. Or maybe you’re working with an influencer to find a completely unexpected way to show what satellite internet makes possible. The challenge is to make it feel authentic, entertaining, and unmistakably Amazon Leo.

After lunch, you switch gears. Our library of footage, photography, animations, and finished content is growing fast. You’re helping build and manage our Digital Asset Management system, keeping everything organized, searchable, and ready for the next project. Because when you’re creating content around the world, finding the right shot shouldn’t take longer than editing it.

By the afternoon, you’re reviewing cuts with a Creative Director, collaborating with designers on a new animation, or experimenting with a social trend to see how it might work for our brand. We believe in cinematic storytelling, even when the finished video is only 15 seconds long. Sometimes the best story is a rocket launching into space. Sometimes it’s a quiet moment with someone getting connected for the first time. The trick is knowing which moments matter.

We’re building a brand that’s equal parts innovative technology and human connection. We want our work to feel thoughtful, surprising, and occasionally a little weird. We don’t want to make content just to fill a calendar. We want to make things people choose to watch.

And we want you to help us figure out what that looks like next.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years of driving compelling creative strategy and execution at an agency or in-house creative team experience
- Experience developing digital campaigns for O&O channels that have global scale
- Experience managing multiple projects and meeting aggressive deadlines
- Knowledge of Adobe Creative software, primarily Premiere, After Effects, Photoshop/Indesign at an advanced level
- Experience with high-volume, high-velocity, large-scale file management (workflow orchestration, file-movement, permission management, etc.)
- Have an online portfolio demonstrating strong visual design skills and advertising experience across a range of media and platforms, along with work that reflects your design process
- Experience with Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems, media libraries, or professional post-production asset management workflows.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in influencer, affiliate marketing
- Experience with asset management, design workflows, or partnering with creative teams
- Experience conveying complex technical concepts to both technical and business audiences
- Experience with online content, multimedia, analytics and impact measurements
- Experience building workflow automation and scripting (Python, AppleScript, or similar) to streamline handoffs, eliminate repetitive editorial tasks, and accelerate project turnarounds
- Experience building custom shortcuts, macros, NLE extensions, or integration panels that enhance editing capabilities
- Experience designing and managing automated ingest, proxy generation, transcoding, and delivery pipelines to remove manual media management bottlenecks
- Experience developing, implementing, or improving Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems, including iconik, Bynder, Frame.io, Wiredrive, or similar platforms

title: Principal Applied Scientist, Items and Relationships Platform
descriptionHtml:
Interested in setting the scientific vision for how every product at Amazon is understood, identified, and connected, with the opportunity to impact every Amazon customer and every selling partner?

The Items and Relationships Platform is the foundation that establishes what every product in Amazon’s catalog is and how products relate to one another. We are rebuilding the platform to establish identity and relationships from meaning and context, using multimodal large language models and generative AI. This is a foundational problem: understanding products deeply enough to identify them, relate them, and keep the catalog trustworthy as it scales to the full breadth of Amazon’s global contribution traffic.

A Principal Applied Scientist on the Items and Relationships Platform owns the science direction for product identity and product relationships. It spans how contributions are resolved into a committed product identity, how products are connected into structural relationships (variations, multipacks, newer versions, lines of products, bundles), how confident those decisions are, and how their quality is measured. You will own the strategy for multimodal understanding, representation learning, relationship inference, calibration, and evaluation, so that science capability compounds across identity and relationships rather than being built one use case at a time.

This role lives at the intersection of research and production. Product identity and relationships are fundamentally an entity resolution problem: deciding what is the same product, and how different products relate, across diverse sources, languages, and formats. You will make the hard modeling calls on where sameness ends and relatedness begins, how models express and calibrate confidence, and how the platform measures quality when there is no external ground truth.

Successful candidates are passionate about translating ambiguous business goals into a coherent science roadmap that enables many businesses at once. You are comfortable being the final scientific arbiter on hard cross-team decisions, and working alongside top-notch applied scientists and software engineers to turn advanced research into production systems.

Key job responsibilities
As a Principal Applied Scientist on the Items and Relationships Platform, you will:

- Own the science direction for product identity: define how products are semantically understood, resolved, and committed as coherent identities, navigating the precision/recall and friction/selection trade-offs inherent in every decision

- Build representations that decide both sameness and typed relatedness, and drive relationship inference from semantic identity rather than one pipeline per relationship type

- Own structural relationship science across variations, multipacks and base products, newer versions, lines of products, and bundles, and discover new relationship types from the gap between defined policy and what identity reveals

- Own calibration and evaluation science: define how models emit calibrated confidence, and build the LLM judge methodology and Catalog Identity Quality metric that measure identity and relationship quality at catalog scale

- Partner with Principal Engineers on cost-aware modeling (cascades, distillation, routing) and close the loop from production signals and corrections back into training

- Set science direction partnering with ACCS Applied Science teams, mentoring senior and principal-track scientists, and driving the documentation and publication of scientific innovation

A day in the life
On a typical day, you move between setting science direction and going deep on hard problems: reviewing a multimodal identity model or a relationship inference experiment with scientists, deciding how a borderline case (a multipack, a newer version, a near-identical variant) should be modeled, and pressure-testing whether a quality gain is real by examining the judge and its calibration. You also spend time zoomed out, shaping the longer-term science roadmap, aligning with Principal Engineers and partner teams on the identity and relationship signals they consume, and mentoring scientists as they take on the ambiguous, high-impact problems that define the platform’s future.

About the team
The Items and Relationships Platform advances state-of-the-art GenAI to deeply understand, uniquely identify, and meaningfully connect every product at Amazon scale. We build the canonical product identity, matching, and relationship systems that power Amazon’s universal catalog: eliminating duplicates, preventing abuse, keeping product families coherent, and integrating the world’s product data to power agentic shopping and trusted discovery for customers worldwide. We solve foundational challenges including schema-agnostic multimodal understanding, relationship inference, evaluation without ground truth, and efficient inference at reduced cost.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of hands-on work in predictive modeling and analysis experience
- PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field
- Experience working in predictive modeling and analysis
- Experience distilling informal customer requirements into problem definitions, dealing with ambiguity and competing objectives
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience with leading experienced scientists as well as having a record of developing junior members from academia or industry to a career track in a business environment

Preferred qualifications

- 10+ years of relevant work in industry or academia experience
- Knowledge of problem solving, algorithm design and complexity analysis
- Experience creating novel algorithms and advancing the state of the art
- Have peer-reviewed scientific contributions in premier journals and conferences

descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. The APJC Data Center Capacity Delivery (DCCD) Construction PMO is looking for a Cost Program Manager to own and mature cost management as a discipline across the full data center project lifecycle. This role covers both Pre-Construction and Construction and drives cost initiatives at the DCCD organisational level.

You won’t control cost on a single project. You will build and govern the system that our cost teams work within: the processes, standards, data, tools, reporting and training behind cost planning and cost control across Asia Pacific. You will support Pre-Construction Cost Planners, Cost Control Cost Engineers and Construction Managers, and work closely with Global Cost Control, Global Tooling, Procurement and Finance. The ideal candidate knows construction cost well, has a strong bias toward automation and standardisation, and can lead change across multiple teams and regions.

Key job responsibilities
Cost Management Manual: Lead the revamp of the Cost Management Manual and maintain in the long term. Make processes more regionally focused while keeping the alignment with global processes to support upstream reporting.

Global BID template: Revamp and standardise the global BID template so cost control teams work from an agreed baseline, with flexibility for regional breakdowns.

Cost reporting: Restructure and automate Quarterly Business Review and Monthly Business Review cost reporting, aligned globally reporting to VP level.

Cost planning, estimating and control tool: Develop an end-to-end tool in phases, starting with a repository of BAFO and Final Cost data integrated with the Procurement Platform. This gives Cost Planners historical averages to build estimates at DD and early design and set the Budget.

DCCD and Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD) cost initiatives: Support DCCD and DCPD cost initiatives and lead cost-related discussions at DCCD level.

Legacy tool deprecation: Lead the retirement of legacy tools to reduce tool fragmentation and maintenance effort.

Integrated financial management tool: Partner with Global Tooling and Cost Control to deliver an integrated financial management tool, including integration with the internal financial system.

Change order categories: Revamp change order categorisation. Consolidate the root-cause-of-change taxonomy and standardise categories across tools, so change orders are classified in the same way region-wide and support year-on-year trend analysis.

Cost training and development: Develop and deliver cost training, including setting up the Amazon Learn Cost Training cohort.

Governance: Run cost governance and audit across the region, and give ad-hoc process and tooling support to cost teams.

Metrics: Define, track and report program KPIs, including adoption of standards, data quality, reporting automation and tool rollout milestones.

A day in the life
You might start the day with Cost Planners reviewing how historical BAFO data feeds into a new estimate, then join a Global Tooling working session on the integrated financial management tool. In the afternoon you could be finalising the half-yearly VP cost pack, agreeing change order root-cause categories with Cost Control Engineers, or running a training session for a new cohort. You will use data to tell the business what it shows, earn trust across teams, and push for simpler, automated ways of working.

About the team
The APJC Construction PMO supports data center delivery across Asia Pacific with program governance, schedule and cost management, digital delivery and training. The team stays lean and focuses on automation, standardisation and capability building, so our Construction, Pre-Construction and Cost Control teams can deliver faster and at lower cost. You will work with a global network of Construction Managers, Pre-Construction Managers, Cost Planners, Cost Control Engineers and Program Managers.

- 7+ years of quantity surveying, cost planning, cost management and cost control experience on large, complex projects, including estimating, budgeting and cost control
- Experience using various cost estimating and planning tools, including using BIM models for quantity take-off, conducting market research and building cost planning models that enable early-stage cost forecasts to inform leadership decisions on land selection, design type and build technology
- Experience building cost repositories, rate libraries, benchmarking tools or estimating models

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in identifying, leading, and executing opportunities to improve, automate, standardize or simplify finance or business tools and processes, or experience designing and implementing controls or experience performing audits over financial reporting environment
- Experience developing and implementing training programs

title: Sr. Associate - Quality Analyst, Global Solutions & Risk Compliance (GSRC)
descriptionHtml:
The Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) organization is a component of Amazon's operations, dedicated to ensuring the compliance of its products and services worldwide. GSRC's core mission is to keep customers, partners, and associates safe while protecting the company from legal and regulatory risks. With a diverse global team spanning across India, China, Poland, Romania, Netherlands, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica, GSRC partners with its stakeholders to classify products and ensure regulatory and legal compliance for product listings. GSRC raises the bar on quality by implementing operational changes matching the everchanging regulatory space. The team designs global, consistent, and scalable solutions and prioritize a blend between technology-driven and human decision-making processes. GSRC believes that innovation thrives on diversity, fostering an inclusive and equitable culture that empowers employees with opportunities for learning and development.

Key job responsibilities
Your job responsibilities as a Sr. Compliance Associate-Quality Analyst may include:
• Performs quality audits on a daily basis using Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and achieves self-utilization, productivity and quality as per defined targets.
• Must be able to comprehend SOPs with minimal support and identify opportunities.
• Identifies anomalies through audits (SOP defects, Process gaps etc.).
• Uses knowledge and identifies defect/s & preliminary root causes, explains the rationale
• Proposes solutions on quality/productivity and work on milestones with managers
• Expertise in research – finding specific information (eg: products, regulations etc) in a timely manner.
• Prepares key insight trends and share reports on regular basis.
• Provide feedbacks to the associates and close loop on audit observations.
• Respond to stakeholders with guidance and flags any updates to Lead/Manager

About the team
Amazon is an E-commerce and Cloud Computing company with headquarters in Seattle, Washington. Since 1995, Amazon has focused on being “the world’s most customer centric company.” Our customers are worldwide, and include not just consumers, but also our sellers and vendors (selling partners). World-class retail brands and individual sellers increase their sales and reach new customers by leveraging the power of the Amazon e-commerce platform. To meet our selling partners’ needs, our smart, diverse, customer-obsessed employees are constantly innovating and building on new ideas.
The Operational Risk Compliance (ORC) organization exists to keep our customers and partners safe, protect associates, and ensure legal and regulatory compliance. We coordinate the aspects of product transactions that are regulated (distribution, shipping, sale, and import/export). Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) is the operational arm of the ORC organization. This involves analyzing product import documentation and flagging hazardous risks. We are also responsible for keeping Amazon customers safe and informed by coordinating actions around worldwide program teams to classify products and ensure Amazon’s product listings follow regulatory and legal compliance guidelines. These actions include removing products from the site and from our warehouses, and contacting customers with pertinent sustainability information. The ORC team partners with GSRC supports regulatory compliance requirements for Amazon’s worldwide programs such as Dangerous Goods, Chemical Safety Compliance, Global Trade Services, Transport Risk Compliance, Sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility and Food Safety. GSRC has offices across India, China, Poland, Romania, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica and supports compliance related needs for worldwide Amazon marketplaces.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience with Microsoft Office products and applications
- 2+ year work experience in Business Process Outsourcing in any of the following domains: accounting, regulatory compliance, IT services, quality assurance

title: Principal Technical Program Manager, MADS
descriptionHtml:
Every day, advertisers and partners worldwide measure the success of their Amazon Ads campaigns through the data Programmatic Reporting delivers: billions of aggregated datapoints that AI agents, machine learning models, and analytics engines around the world now depend on as AI reshapes how advertising is planned and optimized. The Measurement, Ad Tech, and Data Science (MADS) organization at Amazon Ads is looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to drive the largest, most cross-cutting programs behind that data.

Programmatic Reporting owns Amazon Marketing Stream and the Reporting APIs, the interfaces advertisers and partners worldwide use to consume Amazon Ads measurement data. Behind them sit the pipelines that source, transform, and deliver that data, processing billions of aggregated datapoints on Apache Spark, Apache Iceberg, and AWS. Delivering this data accurately, freshly, and cost-efficiently requires programs that span multiple engineering teams, product management, and partner organizations across several sites and regions.

You take on the programs that don't yet have a shape, where the strategy is still forming, the right sequencing isn't obvious, and what success even looks like has to be defined before anything can be planned. You bring order to that ambiguity across the many engineering, product, science, and partner teams spread over multiple sites and regions, and you build the mechanisms that keep delivery predictable at that scale. The guidance, standards, and operating cadence for how these programs run are yours to shape. You operate with real technical depth: you read the designs, ask the sharp question in an architecture review, and, when the direction is wrong, you challenge the strategy, the architecture, or the way the organization is structured to deliver, and back it with a concrete alternative. You do this as a trusted advisor to the organization's senior leaders: you frame the decision, the tradeoff, and your recommendation for audiences that run from the working team all the way up to the organization's most senior leadership, and you help shape where they invest. And you run programs the way this team builds them: instrumented, automated, agent-assisted. Status, rollups, and dependency tracking largely assemble themselves, freeing your own hours for the judgment calls no tool can make. You influence without authority, and you make the teams around you, and yourself, faster.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end delivery of the largest, most ambiguous cross-team programs across pipelines, query engines, APIs, and data integration, where the plan has to be created, not just followed.
- Partner with senior and principal engineers, product leaders, and senior leadership to shape strategy and roadmap in ambiguous spaces, defining what the plan should be, not just executing it.
- Build and sequence the program (scope, milestones, success criteria), and drive resolution of risks, blockers, and dependencies before they slip delivery.
- Establish the operating mechanisms, increasingly automated and agent-driven, that keep delivery predictable across sites and regions.
- Advise senior leaders on where to invest and on the org-wide mechanisms and structure needed to deliver at scale.
- Frame decisions and recommendations for audiences from the working team up to the most senior leaders, with a clear point of view and the data behind it.
- Drive technical tradeoffs across data freshness, accuracy, cost, and time-to-market, escalating crisply when alignment is needed.
- Coordinate launches and deprecations of reporting interfaces across engineering, GTM, partner, and solutions-architecture teams.
- Grow the next tier of leaders: mentor TPMs and engineers, raise the bar on delivery practice, and contribute to hiring and promotion decisions.

About the team
The Programmatic Reporting team builds the data interfaces that power how advertisers and partners measure their Amazon Ads outcomes. We own Amazon Marketing Stream and the Reporting APIs, delivering accurate, consistent, and timely data to advertisers and partners worldwide. Our work sits at the intersection of data engineering and developer experience, and increasingly extends into GenAI-powered interfaces and data lake integrations.

We move fast, think in systems, and obsess over data quality. This role is a chance to take on challenging delivery problems with real room to build the guidance and mechanisms behind them. The team is based in Toronto and partners with teams across multiple sites.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 7+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 5+ years of software development experience
- Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules

title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, Ads Demand Tech Products, Targeting
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Demand Tech products helps marketers, sellers, and app developers promote their products across mobile, connected TV (CTV), and the open internet at scale. You will own the targeting strategy for our Display, Video, and Audio ad buying system, deciding which audiences an advertiser reaches and why, and you will do it as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes how shoppers discover and buy. You will lead product and business strategy alongside a team of product managers, engineers, and applied scientists to deliver measurable results for advertisers of all sizes.

Our systems process billions of bid requests daily, combining many shopping and app signal sources to decide whether to show a given ad to a given person at a given moment. Targeting sits at the center of that decision. As shoppers increasingly rely on AI assistants and chat agents to research and transact, the signals that describe intent are noisy and changing quickly. Your job is to build targeting products that interpret this evolving behavior and help advertisers reach the right audiences, including the agent-driven experiences that are becoming part of everyday shopping.

- Define and drive the multi-year strategy for targeting products across the Display, Video, and Audio ad buying system.
- Lead the design, build, and launch of targeting capabilities that use AI and agent-based signals to match advertiser demand to audience intent.
- Partner with advertisers, agencies, publishers, measurement providers, and data providers to improve the quality and reach of our targeting products.
- Lead product ideation, building, and launches across a team of product managers, engineers, and applied scientists working toward a shared customer objective.

title: Software Development Engineer, Ads Analytics & Insights-Fixed
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Ads works with hundreds of thousands of advertisers, each on a different journey — some running their first campaign, others expanding into streaming TV or display, some at risk of slowing down. The Sales AI team builds the machine learning products that tell sales teams where each advertiser is on that journey and what will help them grow. Our segmentation platform models how advertisers mature over time, predicts where each is heading, and identifies the actions most likely to move them forward — shaping how Amazon Ads organizes sales coverage and decides which advertisers receive managed support.

We're now evolving segmentation from describing where advertisers are to recommending what sellers should do: personalized, interpretable recommendations delivered directly in the tools sellers already use, with a feedback loop that measures which actions actually drive advertiser growth. You'll design and deliver the ML platform and data pipelines that take models from experimentation to production, deliver predictions and recommendations reliably to sales systems at scale, and help move from monthly batch outputs toward on-demand insights — working closely with applied scientists, data scientists, and product partners at the intersection of ML, large-scale data systems, and sales productivity.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and operate the ML platform that takes segmentation models from experimentation to production — including feature ingestion, training, batch inference, and model monitoring
- Deliver model outputs — predictions, scores, and recommendations — reliably to downstream sales systems and partner teams, with clear freshness, versioning, and availability guarantees
- Build scalable, automated data pipelines that bring new advertiser and sales engagement signals into the models quickly, with strong data quality checks
- Design and deliver solutions for well-scoped problems where the technical approach isn't yet defined — such as serving predictions on demand or generating explanations for recommendations
- Partner with applied scientists and data scientists to productionize new models, shorten iteration cycles, and make it easy for scientists to ship without heavy engineering support
- Build the instrumentation that captures how sellers use recommendations and what happens next, so the team can measure impact and improve the models
- Deliver your services end to end — testing, deployment, monitoring, operational excellence, and on-call
- Participate in design and code reviews, holding a high bar for quality, security, and reliability
- Mentor teammates and help onboard new engineers

A day in the life
Your morning might start with the scientists on your team, reviewing results from a new model experiment and deciding what it takes to get it into production. In the afternoon, you might design a pipeline for new advertiser signals, review a teammate's code, or agree with a partner team on how they'll consume a recommendation dataset. Some days you'll trace a data quality alert to its source and fix it; others you'll prototype on-demand predictions. You'll spend most of your day hands-on in the code, and see your work shape how sellers engage with advertisers.

About the team
Sales AI is part of Amazon Ads. We're a team of software engineers, applied scientists, data scientists, and product managers who build the machine learning products behind how Amazon Ads understands advertisers and supports them through sales. Our segmentation models already inform how sales coverage is organized, and we're now extending that work into recommendations that sellers use every day. Engineers and scientists here work as one team: we take ideas from experiment to production together, and we judge success by how our work changes seller actions and advertiser growth — not by model metrics alone.

- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience

title: Risk Specialist I, EAP
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP) team is responsible for ensuring that Amazon's global operation is the benchmark for environmental excellence across all similar industries. EAP transforms environmental regulatory compliance into a zero-defect process through simple, scalable, and sustainable solutions that protect the business, our communities, and the environment.

The Risk Specialist I drives regulated waste compliance across the 2-4 sites they support. This specialist executes the organization's environmental compliance plans at the site level, tracks waste compliance obligations to closure, and partners with site and operations teams to meet compliance milestones. They conduct site inspections, maintain hazardous waste accumulation and manifesting records, and surface gaps through regular program controls.

The ideal candidate brings working knowledge of regulated waste requirements, including RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules. They communicate technical compliance requirements clearly to site leaders, operations partners, and legal stakeholders, and use data to find gaps, prioritize fixes, and improve conformance across their sites.

This role requires sound independent judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to run the right mechanisms and manage competing priorities to meet compliance objectives in a dynamic, high-pace operations environment. If you are motivated by solving regulatory compliance problems in the field, this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the execution and delivery of regulated waste compliance projects and activities, including developing standard operating procedures, workflows, and inspection routines, to mitigate identified risks across the sites you support.
- Apply risk management methods such as waste compliance audits and site inspections to monitor compliance thresholds, test controls, and take corrective action when findings arise.
- Collaborate with site teams, compliance operations, and operations partners to understand business needs, clarify waste compliance requirements, and drive productive discussions that build consensus.
- Identify process improvement opportunities and work with process owners to improve conformance, reduce risk, and increase operational efficiency.
- Prepare clear and concise documentation, including status reports, audit results, metrics, and project communications, so the right information reaches the right audience at the right time.
- Travel expected up to 50% of the time.

A day in the life
Your morning might begin by reviewing incoming risk-related requests and prioritizing your project tasks. You will spend time conducting audits or risk assessments, updating documentation, and coordinating with compliance operations and partner teams. Throughout the day, you will track project milestones, resolve roadblocks, and communicate progress to stakeholders. You will also look for ways to streamline existing processes and ensure your risk area stays aligned with current regulations and team objectives.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to protecting Amazon's customers and business by proactively managing risk across a broad range of areas, from regulatory compliance to operational resilience. We work closely with legal, operations, and business partners to deliver practical risk solutions and build a strong culture of compliance. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and creative problem-solving, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where every team member can grow and make an impact.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) or related field
- 2+ years of experience in environmental compliance, regulated waste management, or workplace risk investigations
- Experience interpreting and applying environmental regulations (RCRA, DOT, and applicable state hazardous waste rules)
- Experience collecting and analyzing data to identify compliance gaps and drive corrective actions

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel
- 4+ years of compliance program management, legal, governance, audit, risk/loss prevention, or equivalent experience
- Experience managing a regulated waste program across multiple sites, including hazardous waste accumulation, manifesting, and disposal
- Hazardous waste certification such as RCRA or DOT (49 CFR) training, or 40-hour HAZWOPER
- Experience conducting site audits or inspections and tracking findings to closure
- Master's degree in Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) or related field

title: Senior Delivery Consultant, Emerging Tech
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Web Services Professional Services (ProServe) team is seeking a skilled Senior Delivery Consultant to join our team at Amazon Web Services (AWS). In this role, you'll work closely with customers to design, implement, and manage AWS solutions that meet their technical requirements and business objectives. You'll be a key player in driving customer success through their cloud journey, providing technical expertise and best practices throughout the project lifecycle.

You bring deep solutions implementation and delivery understanding of Physical AI's building blocks (AI for automation, digital twin, robotics, edge solutions, simulation, and autonomous systems) as well as supply chain technologies. Architecting and deploying autonomous systems, robotics, simulation, digital twins, and industrial AI workloads on AWS, you'll provide secure, reliable, and scalable Physical AI infrastructure for customer innovation. You also bring a background in manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, fulfillment, and the larger supply chain landscape, helping enterprise customers plan and implement the technologies to design, operate, and transform their sourcing, production, transportation, and delivery networks. You'll work with stakeholders to gather requirements, assess current infrastructure, and propose effective migration strategies to AWS, ensuring adherence to best practices, optimizing performance, and managing risks throughout the project.

The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides assistance through a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. We also deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries.


Key job responsibilities
- Providing subject matter expertise on manufacturing supply chains including warehousing, logistics, fulfillment, and production-line transformation, conducting on-site assessments, identifying automation opportunities, and building customer trust through demonstrated domain knowledge
- Owning end-to-end architecture for Physical AI solutions on AWS, including simulation, digital twin, and synthetic data pipelines (e.g., NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Omniverse, OpenUSD, AWS IoT TwinMaker, SiteWise), cloud and edge ML pipelines, and enterprise integration, and guiding delivery from lab through pilot, production, and multi-site rollout
- Designing, training, and deploying autonomy and perception systems across cloud and edge, including fleet data loops, robot policies (imitation and reinforcement learning, vision-language-action models) on SageMaker, edge inference (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson, TensorRT), ROS 2 or equivalent autonomy stacks, and integration with PLC/SCADA, OPC UA, MQTT, WMS/MES, and fleet management systems
- Conducting hazard analysis and building safety cases for machines operating near people, defining test plans and autonomy KPIs (stopping distance, localization error, intervention rate, pick success rate, cycle time), running closed-course and pilot-site trials, and delivering runbooks, operator training, and handoff
- Developing packaged offerings, delivery accelerators, reference architectures, demos, and training materials, and supporting pre-sales with AWS field teams and Physical AI Business Development teams

A day in the life
This team partners with our customers to assist in innovation within their business using AWS Emerging Technologies.

One week you are on a customer site with a laptop and a CAN sniffer, bringing up a new sensor stack on an autonomous vehicle and running closed-course brake tests. The next week you are in Isaac Sim randomizing lighting and textures to close a perception gap, pushing a retrained TensorRT engine to a hardware nodes fleet through Greengrass, and reviewing the safety case with the customer before pilot. Between engagements you turn what you learned into reference architectures the practice can reuse.

About the team
You'll join the AWS North American Professional Services (ProServe) Shared Delivery Team's Emerging Tech practice, a team focused on helping customers realize solutions with emerging and advanced technologies on AWS. We work directly with customers to solve their solution needs and you'll collaborate with cross-functional teams including specialists, solution architects, data scientists, and engineers. Our team values hands-on builders who are curious about the intersection of business and digital systems, and we're committed to creating an environment where every team member can grow, contribute, and innovate.

ABOUT AWS:
 
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
 
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud. 

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. 

10046

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of cloud based solution (AWS or equivalent), system, network and operating system experience
- 5+ years of hands-on experience building and deploying robotics, autonomous systems, or industrial automation (for example AMR/AGV, robotic arms, autonomous vehicles, drones, humanoids, legged robots, or production-line automation systems)
- Experience with ROS 2 or equivalent robotics middleware
- Bachelor's degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Electrical/Computer/Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience
- Experience programming in Python and C++

Preferred qualifications

- AWS Professional level certification
- 3+ years implementing Physical AI projects such as digital twin or simulation environments, robot policy or perception model training, autonomous system deployment, ROS 2 or equivalent robotics middleware integration, or edge inference on Jetson-class hardware
- Delivery experience across two or more of: warehouse or production-line automation, AMR/AGV or robotic-arm deployment, autonomous vehicle or drone deployment, industrial digital twin or simulation, edge AI and computer vision, OT integration, or supply chain and manufacturing optimization
- Familiarity with the AWS Physical AI stack (Physical AI Toolchain on AWS, IoT Core, Greengrass v2, SiteWise, TwinMaker, SageMaker, Bedrock, Kinesis Video Streams, S3/Glue/Athena, EKS or Batch, CDK) and the NVIDIA robotics stack (Isaac Sim/Lab/ROS, Omniverse, OpenUSD, Jetson, TensorRT, CUDA)
- Experience with autonomy and sim-to-real: perception, SLAM and localization, pose estimation, GNSS/IMU fusion with RTK corrections, NAV2, MoveIt, kinematics, trajectory optimization, real-time control, sensor fusion, multi-sensor calibration, domain randomization, and transfer validation on real hardware
- Experience with hardware and industrial integration: LiDAR, cameras, GNSS/IMU, force/torque sensors, end-effectors and actuators, CAN/drive-by-wire, PLC/I/O, E-stop; protocols such as OPC UA, Modbus, PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, MQTT with PLC/SCADA, MES, WMS, or ERP; and connectivity over private/public 5G, Wi-Fi, and satellite/NTN links including secure device-to-cloud (MQTT, VPN) and real-time correction/telemetry streams
- Experience with robotics safety standards (for example ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, ISO 3691-4/ANSI R15.08, ISO 13849/IEC 62061, ISO 26262) and OT/IoT security (device identity, secure OTA, OT/IT segmentation)
